questions.q: How many surahs are in the Quran?
questions.info: The Quran has 114 surahs and more than 6,200 ayahs. Surahs are classed as Meccan or Medinan, by when and where they were revealed.

questions.q: Which surah opens the Quran?
questions.info: Al-Fatiha means "The Opening". It is recited in every rak'ah of prayer, which is why it is also called Umm al-Kitab — "the Mother of the Book".

questions.q: Which is the longest surah?
questions.info: Surah Al-Baqarah ("The Cow") has 286 ayahs. It contains Ayat al-Kursi and the longest ayah of the Quran, about recording debts (2:282).

questions.q: Which is the shortest surah?
questions.info: Surah Al-Kawthar has three short ayahs. Al-Kawthar is the name of a river in Paradise granted to the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: In which month did the revelation of the Quran begin?
questions.info: This is stated in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:185). The revelation began on the Night of Decree and continued for about 23 years.

questions.q: Which angel brought the revelation to the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.info: The angel Jibril (peace be upon him) conveyed revelation to the prophets. The Quran also calls him "the Trustworthy Spirit" (26:193).

questions.q: Where was the first revelation given to the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.info: The cave of Hira is on Mount Nur near Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ used to retreat there for worship even before his prophethood.

questions.q: With which word does the first revelation begin?
questions.info: The first verses revealed were the opening ayahs of Surah Al-Alaq (96:1–5) — about reading in the name of the Lord who created man.

questions.q: In which surah is Ayat al-Kursi?
questions.info: Ayat al-Kursi is the 255th ayah of Surah Al-Baqarah. It speaks of Allah's greatness, His knowledge and His dominion over the heavens and the earth.

questions.q: Which ayah did the Prophet ﷺ call the greatest in the Quran?
questions.info: This is reported in a hadith from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, narrated by Muslim. Ayat al-Kursi is commonly recited after the obligatory prayers and before sleep.

questions.q: Which surah does not begin with "Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim"?
questions.info: The ninth surah, At-Tawbah ("Repentance"), is the only one without the basmala at its start. It is also called Bara'ah ("Disavowal").

questions.q: In which surah does the basmala appear twice?
questions.info: In Surah An-Naml the basmala appears at the start and in ayah 30 — in Prophet Sulayman's letter to the Queen of Sheba. So the Quran has 114 basmalas, one per surah.

questions.q: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ say equals a third of the Quran?
questions.info: This is reported in a hadith narrated by al-Bukhari. Surah Al-Ikhlas ("Sincerity") is devoted entirely to the oneness of Allah — tawhid.

questions.q: Which surah is named after a woman?
questions.info: Maryam, the mother of Prophet Isa, is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran. The 19th surah bears her name.

questions.q: How many ayahs are in Surah Al-Fatiha?
questions.info: Al-Fatiha has seven ayahs. The Quran calls it "the seven oft-repeated" (15:87) because it is repeated in every rak'ah.

questions.q: Who was the first human and the first prophet?
questions.info: Adam (peace be upon him) was the first human created by Allah and the first prophet. All people descend from him and his wife Hawwa.

questions.q: Which prophet built the ark?
questions.info: Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) called his people to worship one God for many years. By Allah's command he built the ark and was saved from the flood with the believers.

questions.q: Who built the Kaaba together with his son Ismail?
questions.info: This is mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:127). Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them) raised the Kaaba and prayed that Allah would accept their work.

questions.q: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish?
questions.info: From inside the fish, Prophet Yunus (peace be upon him) called on Allah, affirming His oneness and admitting his own mistake. His supplication (21:87) is still recited in hard times.

questions.q: To which prophet was the Tawrat revealed?
questions.info: The Tawrat (Torah) is the scripture revealed to Prophet Musa (peace be upon him). Belief in all the scriptures revealed by Allah is a pillar of faith.

questions.q: To which prophet was the Zabur revealed?
questions.info: The Zabur (Psalms) was revealed to Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him). Dawud was both a prophet and a ruler, and Allah gave him a beautiful voice.

questions.q: To which prophet was the Injil revealed?
questions.info: The Injil (Gospel) was revealed to Prophet Isa (peace be upon him), the son of Maryam. Muslims believe Isa is a messenger of Allah and that Allah raised him up.

questions.q: To which prophet did Allah subject the wind and the jinn?
questions.info: Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him) was given an unmatched kingdom: the wind and the jinn obeyed him, and he understood the speech of birds and ants.

questions.q: Which prophet is known for his patience in a long illness?
questions.info: Prophet Ayyub (peace be upon him) lost his health, wealth and children, yet never complained. Allah healed him and restored his blessings — his patience became an example for believers.

questions.q: Who was the father of Prophet Yusuf?
questions.info: Yusuf was the son of Prophet Yaqub, the grandson of Ishaq and the great-grandson of Ibrahim (peace be upon them all). Yaqub is also known as Israil.

questions.q: Which prophet was thrown into a well by his brothers?
questions.info: The story of Yusuf is told in the 12th surah, which bears his name. The Quran calls it the best of stories (12:3).

questions.q: Who was Prophet Musa's brother and also a prophet?
questions.info: Musa asked Allah to make his brother Harun his helper, because Harun was more eloquent. Allah answered his prayer (20:29–36).

questions.q: Who was the son of Prophet Zakariya and also a prophet?
questions.info: Allah gave Zakariya his son Yahya in old age, when his wife was barren. No one had borne that name before Yahya (19:7).

questions.q: How many prophets are named in the Quran?
questions.info: Usually 25 prophets are counted as named in the Quran. There were many more prophets — Allah did not tell us about all of them (40:78).

questions.q: Who is the last prophet?
questions.info: The Quran calls Muhammad ﷺ "the Seal of the Prophets" (33:40). There will be no prophet after him, and the Quran is the final scripture.

questions.q: In which city was the Prophet ﷺ born?
questions.info: The Prophet ﷺ was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant — around 570 CE. He was from the clan of Hashim of the Quraysh tribe.

questions.q: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ mother?
questions.info: His mother was Aminah bint Wahb. She passed away when the Prophet ﷺ was about six; his father, Abdullah, had died before he was born.

questions.q: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ wet nurse?
questions.info: It was an Arab custom to send infants to wet nurses in the desert. The Prophet ﷺ spent his early childhood with Halimah of the Banu Sa'd tribe.

questions.q: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ first wife?
questions.info: Khadijah (may Allah be pleased with her) was the first to believe in his prophethood and supported him through the hardest years.

questions.q: How old was the Prophet ﷺ when the revelation began?
questions.info: The revelation began when the Prophet ﷺ was 40. Before that, people in Makkah called him al-Amin — "the trustworthy".

questions.q: How long did the prophetic mission last?
questions.info: The Prophet ﷺ called people to Islam for about 13 years in Makkah and about 10 years in Madinah. He passed away in 11 AH at the age of 63.

questions.q: What is the migration of the Muslims from Makkah to Madinah called?
questions.info: The Hijrah took place in 622 CE. In Madinah, then called Yathrib, the first Muslim community took shape.

questions.q: From which event is the Islamic calendar counted?
questions.info: The Hijri calendar was introduced under Caliph Umar. It is lunar, so it shifts about 11 days each year relative to the solar calendar.

questions.q: Who accompanied the Prophet ﷺ during the Hijrah?
questions.info: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) hid with the Prophet ﷺ in the cave of Thawr for three days. This is mentioned in the Quran (9:40).

questions.q: What is the Prophet's ﷺ night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem called?
questions.info: Al-Isra is the night journey to Jerusalem, and al-Mi'raj is the ascension to the heavens. It was then that the five daily prayers were prescribed.

questions.q: What was the first major battle of the Muslims?
questions.info: The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan, 2 AH. About 313 Muslims defeated an army three times their size.

questions.q: Who was the first muezzin in Islam?
questions.info: Bilal was enslaved in Makkah and tortured for his faith until Abu Bakr freed him. The Prophet ﷺ chose him to call the adhan for his beautiful, strong voice.

questions.q: Where is the Prophet ﷺ buried?
questions.info: The Prophet ﷺ is buried in Madinah, in Aishah's room, which is now inside the Prophet's Mosque. Abu Bakr and Umar are buried beside him.

questions.q: Who was the first rightly guided caliph?
questions.info: After the Prophet ﷺ passed away, Abu Bakr as-Siddiq became the first caliph. There were four rightly guided caliphs: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali.

questions.q: How many pillars does Islam have?
questions.info: The five pillars of Islam: the shahadah, prayer, zakat, fasting in Ramadan, and Hajj for those who are able.

questions.q: How many pillars of iman (faith) are there?
questions.info: Belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day and divine decree. They are listed in the well-known hadith of Jibril.

questions.q: How many obligatory prayers are there each day?
questions.info: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. The five prayers were prescribed on the night of the Mi'raj.

questions.q: How many rak'ahs are in the obligatory Fajr prayer?
questions.info: The obligatory part of Fajr is two rak'ahs. Two sunnah rak'ahs are prayed before it — the Prophet ﷺ almost never left them.

questions.q: How many rak'ahs are in the obligatory Maghrib prayer?
questions.info: Maghrib is the only obligatory prayer with three rak'ahs. It is prayed after sunset.

questions.q: How many rak'ahs are in Dhuhr, Asr and Isha (when not travelling)?
questions.info: Dhuhr, Asr and Isha have four rak'ahs each. A traveller may shorten them to two.

questions.q: What is the minor ablution before prayer called?
questions.info: In wudu you wash the face, the arms to the elbows, wipe the head and wash the feet to the ankles (5:6). Ghusl is the full ablution of the whole body.

questions.q: What is done instead of ablution when there is no water?
questions.info: Tayammum is purification with clean earth when there is no water or it cannot be used. It is mentioned in the Quran (4:43, 5:6).

questions.q: What is the call to prayer called?
questions.info: The adhan calls people to prayer, and the iqamah is the second call right before it starts. In the Fajr adhan the words "Prayer is better than sleep" are added.

questions.q: Which direction do Muslims face in prayer?
questions.info: The direction of the Kaaba is called the qibla. You can find it in the Qibla section of this app.

questions.q: What was the first qibla of the Muslims?
questions.info: For about 16–17 months after the Hijrah, Muslims prayed towards Al-Aqsa in Jerusalem. Then the qibla was changed to the Kaaba (2:144).

questions.q: What is the obligatory annual charity on wealth called?
questions.info: Zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam. It is usually 2.5% of savings that have reached the nisab and been held for a year.

questions.q: Which charity is paid at the end of Ramadan, before the Eid prayer?
questions.info: Zakat al-Fitr is paid for oneself and one's family so that the poor can celebrate too. It must be given before the Eid prayer.

questions.q: What is the pre-dawn meal during fasting called?
questions.info: Suhur is the meal before dawn, and iftar is breaking the fast after sunset. The Prophet ﷺ said there is barakah in suhur.

questions.q: On which day is the Jumu'ah prayer held?
questions.info: The Friday prayer replaces Dhuhr and is preceded by a sermon — the khutbah. Friday is the best day of the week for Muslims.

questions.q: How many circuits are made in tawaf around the Kaaba?
questions.info: Tawaf is walking around the Kaaba seven times anticlockwise. It begins at the corner of the Black Stone.

questions.q: Between which hills is sa'i performed?
questions.info: Sa'i recalls Hajar, who searched for water for little Ismail, running seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah (2:158).

questions.q: In which month is Hajj performed?
questions.info: The main rites of Hajj take place from the 8th to the 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah. The Day of Arafah is the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

questions.q: Which month of the Islamic calendar is Ramadan?
questions.info: Ramadan is the ninth month, followed by Shawwal. The Islamic calendar has 12 lunar months.

questions.q: Which night is better than a thousand months?
questions.info: This is stated in Surah Al-Qadr (97:3). It is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan, especially the odd ones.

questions.q: Which holiday is celebrated at the end of Ramadan?
questions.info: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated on the 1st of Shawwal with the Eid prayer. The second holiday, Eid al-Adha, falls on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

questions.q: What is the spring near the Kaaba called?
questions.info: The spring of Zamzam appeared by Allah's mercy when Hajar was searching for water for her son Ismail. It has not dried up for thousands of years.

questions.q: What does "SubhanAllah" mean?
questions.info: With these words we glorify Allah and declare Him free of any imperfection. After prayer it is customary to say it 33 times.

questions.q: What does "Alhamdulillah" mean?
questions.info: Muslims thank Allah with these words in every situation — in joy and in hardship. They open Al-Fatiha after the basmala.

questions.q: What does "Allahu Akbar" mean?
options: There is no god but Allah
questions.info: Every prayer begins with these words — the takbir. They are also said in the adhan and on the days of Eid.

questions.q: What does "InshaAllah" mean?
questions.info: When speaking about the future, Muslims add "InshaAllah" (18:23–24). "MashaAllah" — "what Allah has willed" — is said when admiring something.

questions.q: What does "Astaghfirullah" mean?
questions.info: This is istighfar — asking for forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ asked Allah for forgiveness more than seventy times a day.

questions.q: What does the word "sabr" mean?
questions.info: Sabr is patience and steadfastness: in worship, in avoiding sin and in trials. The Quran says that Allah is with the patient (2:153).

questions.q: What does the word "shukr" mean?
questions.info: Shukr is gratitude to Allah with the heart, words and deeds. Allah promised to give more to those who are grateful (14:7).

questions.q: What does the word "niyyah" mean?
questions.info: A well-known hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim begins by saying that deeds are judged by intentions. A good intention turns an ordinary act into worship.

questions.q: What does the word "barakah" mean?
questions.info: Barakah is the blessing and benefit Allah places in time, wealth and deeds. Even a little with barakah brings much good.

questions.q: What does the word "Islam" mean?
questions.info: Islam means submission to the one God. The word comes from the same root as "salam" — peace.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Ikhlas:
questions.info: Surah Al-Ikhlas, ayahs 1–2. As-Samad means the Self-Sufficient: everyone needs Him, and He needs no one.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Fatiha:
questions.info: Surah Al-Fatiha, ayahs 2–3. Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim are names of Allah that speak of His mercy.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Fatiha:
questions.info: Surah Al-Fatiha, ayah 5: we worship Allah alone and ask for help from Him alone.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Asr:
questions.info: Surah Al-Asr, ayahs 1–2. Imam ash-Shafi'i said that if people reflected only on this surah, it would be enough for them.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Falaq:
questions.info: Surah Al-Falaq, ayahs 1–2. Together with Surah An-Nas it is called al-Mu'awwidhatayn — the two surahs of seeking Allah's protection.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah An-Nas:
questions.info: Surah An-Nas, ayahs 1–2. It is the last surah of the Quran; the Prophet ﷺ recited it with Al-Ikhlas and Al-Falaq before sleep.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Kawthar:
questions.info: Surah Al-Kawthar, ayahs 1–2: in gratitude for the blessing given — pray to your Lord and offer sacrifice for Him.
